name: Data Product
purpose: Represent a governed data product and immutable product versions, with a separately identified catalog record describing each product head or version, without absorbing dataset, distribution, interface, execution, observation, assessment, offering or agreement lifecycles.

owns: immutable published product versions and successor lineage
product purpose, consumer scope and bounded use cases
non-owning resource composition by role and resolution policy
access-route declarations and pinned contract references
measurable product promises and declared aggregation rules
separately rooted product-scoped Catalog Record identity and lifecycle
separately rooted effective-dated ConsumerEntitlementBinding objects that reference external terms and access authority
delegates: dataset, dataset-version and distribution identity to WM-DAT-001
schema and data-contract versions to WM-DAT-004
API and interface-contract revisions to WM-SFT-003
pipeline and processing-run execution to WM-ACT-053
market, channel, price and validity offering semantics to the shared Offering authority
legal or commercial agreement lifecycle to the applicable agreement authority
excludes: price, tariff, market and sales-channel lifecycle
agreement, order, subscription, delivery or payment lifecycle

catalogRecordBoundary.rule: WM-DAT-008 owns catalog records only when the described resource is a data product or data-product version. WM-DAT-001 owns catalog records whose described resource is a dataset, dataset series or distribution. Record namespaces and described-resource types must make the two masters disjoint.
catalogRecordBoundary.coexistenceRule: ProductCatalogRecord is a separately rooted WM-DAT-008 object, not a contained DataProduct member. It may predate product completion and survives withdrawal while retaining independent identity and lifecycle.
catalogRecordBoundary.ruleStatus: Declared boundary pending reciprocal WM-DAT-001 amendment; not yet enforced canonically.

resourceComposition.versionRule: Rebinding a pinned member creates a successor. A declared-series-head advance does not, unless it breaches a promise; breach is asserted on the existing version and remediation by repinning or promise revision creates a successor.

consumerEntitlementBinding.classification: separately rooted identified governed object mastered by WM-DAT-008; not contained in DataProduct, not a bare relation, agreement, authorization grant or new model identity
consumerEntitlementBinding.effect: Records the governed consumer-product-version-resource-purpose terms association; it neither creates external terms nor grants access.
consumerEntitlementBinding.identityRule: Identity is stable across status changes; external agreement and product-version references remain independently versioned.
termsRules: terms references are authority-qualified pointers and never inline legal or commercial text
accessAuthorityRef identifies a competent authority and never an access decision

relations.purpose: Resolve datasets, versions, series and distributions without importing their lifecycle.
relations.condition: Required when any resourceComposition member is dataset, dataset-version or distribution.

relations.purpose: Pin schema and data-contract versions and consumer obligations.
Resolve purpose-qualified quality assessments without copying verdict state.
Resolve external measurements supporting product promises.
Pin API or interface-contract revisions for access routes.
Resolve execution evidence without importing run state.

operations.effect: Mint a stable product identity and draft version only after the promotion gate is complete.
Freeze the product version, composition, contract pins, promises and deprecation policy.
Create or revise a separately rooted record describing a product or product version.
operations.authority: catalog operator writes through the WM-DAT-008 record master boundary

operations.effect: Record a separately rooted effective-dated binding to external terms and access authority.
operations.authority: WM-DAT-008 steward records decisions supplied by the competent external authorities

operations.effect: Deprecate, withdraw or retire a Product Version under productLifecycle and notify holders per the deprecation policy.
Apply an allowed Catalog Record transition with statusChangedAt and authority evidence.
operations.authority: catalog operator through WM-DAT-008 record master

operations.effect: Apply an allowed binding transition with required timestamps and decision references.
operations.authority: WM-DAT-008 steward recording external authority decisions

invariants.statement: Catalog Record, Data Product and every composed resource have separate resolvable identities.
A ProductCatalogRecord describes only a Product or Product Version; the reciprocal WM-DAT-001 dataset-record boundary remains held.
Published Product Versions are immutable; any required-content change creates a linked successor.
Every composition member declares role, resource identity, resource type and pinned-versus-head resolution policy.
Rebinding a pinned member creates a successor Product Version.
A declared-series-head advance does not version the Product while promises hold; breach is appended and repin or promise revision creates a successor.
The Product stores no dataset bytes, distributions, pipeline runs, observations or assessment results.
Every access route identifies its interface or distribution at a pinned revision and names its authorization requirement.
Every promise identifies metric definition, target, unit, window, measurement point and aggregation rule.
Consumer terms cite an authority-qualified external agreement or internal-terms reference plus an effective period.
ConsumerEntitlementBinding is separately rooted with stable identity, approval, status history, interval and audit evidence.
Listing, discoverability, availability, authorization, delivery, acceptance, fitness and use are independent assertions.
Product withdrawal never cascades to datasets, services, agreements, Catalog Records or bindings.
A subject missing any promotion-gate element is a catalogued resource, not a Data Product.
One Product may have many Catalog Records; delisting one never retires the Product.
Catalog Record and Product fields and transitions never overwrite across identities.
ConsumerEntitlementBinding is neither agreement nor access grant and never authorizes access by itself.
Distinct consumers may hold distinct bindings to the same Product Version under different external terms.
Catalog Record, Product Version and binding validity intervals advance independently.
Pipeline runs and quality observations never create Product Versions.
Historical Catalog Records and expired bindings remain addressable after Product withdrawal or tombstoning.
No price, tariff, SKU, market, channel, sales term or legal text is stored in WM-DAT-008; only references are held.
Product identity is stable across accountability transfer because mintingNamespace is immutable and distinct from accountableOwnerRef.
A binding productVersionRef always contains productId and productVersionId.
Bindings may become active only for a published non-retired Product Version; later withdrawal does not erase binding history.
Lifecycle transitions conform to the declared transition graphs and terminal-state timestamps are conditionally required.
Deprecation names successor or no-successor, sunset, holder notice policy and notice evidence.
Invariant identifiers are stable, never reused and remain attached to their statement.

holds: Offering and agreement authorities remain identifier-unassigned and are referenced descriptively, never locally mastered.
Candidate relation rows confer no mutation or cascade authority.
External standards and product projections are alignment mappings, not conformance claims.
Grok accepted the boundary with an identified dependent entitlement object; final frozen audit remains to be reconciled.
Catalog Record/Data Product coexistence requires registry-facing dual-identity presentation and must not become a merged type.
Required and conditional relations resolve to models that are not canonically publishable; no canonical layer may rest on this candidate.
The WM-DAT-001 relation and reciprocal Catalog Record boundary are unapproved; requiredness is conditional and provisional.
Disjoint record mastership requires WM-DAT-001 to demote its catalogue-record facet to a reference; until amended this rule is declared, not enforced.
Metric-definition authority is pending EM-DAT-05, so promise references cannot yet be satisfied canonically.
Offering and agreement bindings remain external and identifier-unassigned; references are authority-qualified without placeholder IDs.
Pipeline-definition mastership remains external; a WM-DAT-005 relation is not declared until registry approval.

offeringAgreementPlacement.offering: external commercial master; effective-dated binding only
offeringAgreementPlacement.consumerAgreement: external legal/commercial master; effective-dated binding only
offeringAgreementPlacement.rule: No price, SKU or legal text is copied into WM-DAT-008.

versionTriggers.rule: Any change to required content of a published product version creates an immutable successor. Illustrative cases are non-exhaustive; exclusions are exhaustive.
exhaustiveNoSuccessorCases: advance of a declared-series-head member while all promises remain satisfied

ProductCatalogRecord.masteredBy: WM-DAT-008 for records describing a Data Product or Data Product Version
ProductCatalogRecord.rule: Separately rooted; references Product and may predate completion or survive withdrawal.

ConsumerEntitlementBinding.rule: Separately rooted; references Product Version, consumer and external terms/authorization authorities.

identityRules.mintingNamespace: Immutable identity scope, distinct from current accountableOwnerRef; accountability transfer never changes product identity.
identityRules.productVersionLabel: version is an immutable unique label scoped to productId and is not part of the key.

promiseBreachRule: A head advance that violates a declared promise never mutates the published version; append a promise-breach state and create a successor for any repin or promise revision.

definitions.withdrawn: No new use is offered; historical identity and obligations persist.
definitions.retired: Operational support has ended after withdrawal; records still resolve.

definitions.tombstoned: Identifier remains resolvable while removed content and reason are recorded; never deletion.

productVersionTermsRule: termsAndAuthorizationRefs are descriptive external references and never substitute for a ConsumerEntitlementBinding or mint legal terms.
invariantIdPolicy: Stable and never reused; new invariants append.
